title: Texas Border Officers Catch Fugitive, Stop $557K Heroin Shipment - NewsBreak
text:
By Nick ,
6 hours ago
On two separate occasions, the U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) seized almost 30 pounds of heroin from slipping into the country, along with an arrest made of someone charged with indecency with a child .
Wanted Felon Arrested at Texas Border On September 15, CBP officers at Eagle Pass International Bridge stopped 46-year-old Merlin Martinez , a U.S. citizen, for secondary inspection. After running Martinez through biometric verification, they discovered two outstanding warrants for his arrest.
One warrant was issued by the Bexar County Sheriff’s Office for indecency with a child by sexual contact . The second active warrant was for possession of marijuana out of Maverick County.
Martinez was detained and turned over to the Maverick County Sheriff’s Office to await criminal proceedings.
Massive Heroin Seizure Along Texas Border Just one day prior to the arrest of Merlin Martinez, CBP officers at Laredo Port of Entry intercepted over $557,000 of alleged heroin hidden inside a vehicle.
Laredo Port of Entry Port Director Alberto Flores voiced his support for the drug discovery:
Our frontline CBP officers continue to apply their inspection skills together with the latest technology, and that combination yielded this significant hard narcotics interception.
On September 14, a 63-year-old Mexican citizen driving a 2008 Chrysler Voyager from Mexico into Texas was stopped in Laredo, TX.
Officers referred the man to secondary inspection where further investigation inside his vehicle was conducted, including the use of a canine unit.
Eventually, 12 packages weighing in at 29.05 pounds of alleged heroin were discovered. The total street value of the illegal narcotics was estimated to be $557,237 .
The 8 Most Wanted Men in Texas Have $3K to $7.5K Rewards These eight individuals are highly sought after by Texas authorities. Gallery Credit: Michael Gibson / Townsquare Media Texas Department of Public Safety Stephen Joseph Vess - Up to $3,000 Reward Stephen Joseph Vess is a Texas 10 Most Wanted Fugitive with ties to Rockwall County, Texas, including the city of Mabank. In August 2014, Vess was arrested in Rockwall County for Sexual Assault of a Child and subsequently bonded out. Later that year he failed to appear in court and on November 13, 2014, warrants were issued out of Rockwall County for Vess’ arrest for Sexual Assault of a Child and Possession of Child Pornography. Texas Department of Public Safety Miguel Angel Gomez - Up to $7,500 Reward Miguel Angel Gomez is a convicted sex offender required to register annually. He has ties to Harris County, including the city of Houston, Texas. In 1994, Gomez was convicted of Aggravated Assault with a Deadly Weapon, Burglary of Vehicle, and Burglary of Building. He was subsequently sentenced to 10 years confinement for the Aggravated Assault with a Deadly Weapon and Burglary of Vehicle offenses and sentenced to 7 years confinement for the Burglary of Building offense. In 2009, Gomez was convicted of Sexual Assault of a Child following an incident with a 16-year-old female. He was subsequently sentenced to 15 years confinement. In 2022, a warrant was issued out of Harris County for Gomez’s arrest for Murder. Additionally, on December 13, 2022, the Texas Board of Pardons and Paroles issued a warrant for his arrest for Parole Violation (Original Offense: Sexual Assault of a Child). Texas Department of Public Safety Raul Herrera, Jr. - Up to $7,500 Reward Raul Herrera, Jr., is affiliated with the Tango Vallucos gang and has also been affiliated in the past with the Texas Syndicate gang. In addition to having ties to the Rio Grande Valley area, including McAllen, Herrera also has ties to Mexico. In 1990, Herrera was convicted of two counts of Aggravated Assault and subsequently sentenced to ten years’ confinement. In 2002, he was convicted in federal court of Conspiracy to Possess with the Intent to Distribute Cocaine and Felon in Possession of a Firearm, for which he was sentenced to eleven years’ confinement and nine years’ confinement, served concurrently. In 2014, he was convicted of Money Laundering and subsequently sentenced to three years’ confinement. On May 4, 2023, warrants were issued out of Hidalgo County for Herrera’s arrest for Aggravated Sexual Assault, Aggravated Assault with a Deadly Weapon, Assault Causes Bodily Injury of a Family Member, and Violation of Bond/Protective Order. Texas Department of Public Safety Ernest Christopher Nathan - Up to $5,000 Reward Ernest Christopher Nathan has ties to Harris County, including the city of Houston, Texas. He also has ties to the states of Georgia, Ohio, and Louisiana. In 2006, Nathan was convicted of Purchase/Possess/Control Drug and Aggravated Assault in Georgia and subsequently sentenced to 1 year confinement and 2 years confinement, served concurrently. In 2016, Nathan was convicted of Battery and Bail Jumping in Georgia and subsequently sentenced to 1 year of confinement. On October 4, 2022, Nathan was arrested by Houston Police Department for Murder and Evading Arrest/Detention with a Vehicle. The following day Nathan was released on bond. On February 29, 2024, a warrant was issued for his arrest for Failure to Appear (Original Offense: Murder – Firearm). Texas Department of Public Safety Arthur Dewayne Carson - Up to $5,000 Reward Arthur Dewayne Carson is a Texas 10 Most Wanted Fugitive with ties to Austin, Mexia, Lubbock, and Fort Worth, Texas. In 1991, Carson was convicted of Robbery Causing Bodily Injury and subsequently sentenced to 12 years in TDCJ prison. He was released on parole after several years but was convicted again of Robbery Causing Bodily Injury in 1994. He was subsequently sentenced to 40 years in TDCJ prison. Carson was last released on parole from TDCJ in 2012.On October 18, 2013, the Texas Board of Pardons and Paroles issued a warrant for Carson’s arrest for Parole Violation. Additionally, on September 11, 2014, the Hays County Sheriff’s Office issued a warrant for his arrest for Aggravated Robbery. Carson was last known to be in Austin, Texas, and believed to be homeless. Texas Department of Public Safety Carlos Jose Ayala Morales - Up to $5,000 Reward Carlos Jose Ayala Morales is a convicted sex offender required to register every three months. He has ties to Harris County, including the city of Houston, Texas. In 2000, Ayala Morales was convicted of Burglary of Building and subsequently sentenced to 6 months of confinement. In 2018, Ayala Morales was convicted of Evading Arrest/Detention with a Vehicle and subsequently sentenced to 7 years confinement. Additionally, in 2018 Ayala Morales was convicted of three counts of Indecency with a Child by Sexual Contact following incidents with two 14-year-old girls and one 12-year-old girl. Ayala Morales was also convicted in 2018 of Indecency with a Child by Exposure following an incident with an 8-year-old girl. He was subsequently sentenced to 7 years confinement for each offense to be served concurrently. Ayala Morales was discharged from the Texas Department of Criminal Justice (TDCJ) in 2024. On February 10, 2025, a warrant was issued out of Harris County for his arrest for Attempted Indecency with a Child Sexual Contact. Texas Department of Public Safety Tyler Lee Palmer - Up to $3,000 Reward Tyler Lee Palmer has ties to Archer County including the city of Holliday, Texas. In 2021, Palmer was convicted of four counts of Aggravated Assault Causes Serious Bodily Injury and subsequently sentenced to 5 years’ probation for each offense. In 2022, Palmer was convicted of Possession of Controlled Substance and subsequently sentenced to 3 years’ probation. On May 20, 2025, a warrant was issued out of Wichita County for his arrest for Probation Violation (Original Offenses: Aggravated Assault Causes Bodily Injury (x4) and Possession of Controlled Substance). Texas Department of Public Safety Hector Daniel c - Up to $3,000 Reward Hector Daniel Silva has ties to El Paso County, including the city of Fabens, Texas. In 2023, Silva was convicted of Possession of Controlled Substance. In 2024, Silva was convicted of Prohibited Substance/Item in a Correctional/Civil Commitment Facility. On June 6, 2025, a warrant was issued out of El Paso County for his arrest for Aggravated Kidnapping for Ransom/Reward, Burglary of Habitation with Intent to Commit Other Felony, and Aggravated Robbery.
